newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK MINOAN LINES ORDERS FOSEN $215 MLN FERRIES.
newsitem.headline: GREEK MINOAN LINES ORDERS FOSEN $215 MLN FERRIES.

text.p: Passenger shipper Minoan Lines is investing heavily in the construction of two new high-speed ferries in its Greece-Italy line, it said on Tuesday.
The ships will cost $215 million and will be delivered on January and June of 1998, Minoan said in a statement.
Fosen, the Norwegian shipyard which has undertaken the construction of Minoan's two ships, Ikaros and Pacifai, built the company's first high-speed ferry Aretousa in the summer of 1995.

"Minoan Lines' recent decision to invest in state-of-the-art luxury ships is in line with its five-year business plan to renew and modernise its fleet. The total amount of investment is expected to reach 70 billion drachmas," the statement said.
High-speed ferries will be fast and safe. Their technical characteristics include a gross registered tonnage of 31,000 tonnes and a speed of 27 knots.
These ferries will execute the Patras-Ancona route in 19 hours. Minoan Lines is also thinking of investing in lines connecting Patras with Venice and Brindezi.
Based passenger volume, Minoan Lines' main competitors for its northern route are: Superfast Ferries , Strintzis Lines and ANEK Lines.
In the southern route its two major competitors are Ventouris and Agoudimos.
The southern shipping route is monopolized by Greek coastal operators. The only foreign firm covering the same route is Italy's Adriatica, Minoan Lines officials said.
Minoan Lines launched its new ship Knossos to service southrn routes in October.
For the first ten months of 1996, net profits before depreciation were 6.6 billion drachmas, up 34.3 percent on 1995.

Ikaros and Pacifai's $215 million dollar cost will be covered by a $150 million loan and $65 million in equity, it said. The loan will be syndicated by Citibank's shipping division. --Margarita Sotiropoulou, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
